role: experimental sRGB sailcloth base color; not measured PBR data
processing: copied byte-for-byte from built-in imagegen output
prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset: UV-repeatable sRGB base-color texture for the cloth of a 3D Ming-era sailing ship. Image 1 is the target fabric; image 2 is a palette reference, not a scene to recreate. Change only the cloth's dye: make image 1 distinctly lighter and more faded, a soft dusty terracotta / sun-bleached warm cinnabar with a little natural ochre and muted beige fiber, roughly centered on sRGB #c77c5f. It must be noticeably lighter and less saturated than image 1, not burgundy, crimson or brown; suitable to remain legible when naturally shaded in a 3D game. Keep the straight-on, evenly illuminated woven hemp surface and subtle fiber character; distribute gentle small-scale tonal variation evenly. Full-bleed square seamless-looking flat texture. No large blotches, no gradients, no lighting, no seams, battens, ropes, folds, symbols, ornament, lettering, ship, border or watermark. No glossy paint or artificial plastic.
limitations: UV repeat, aliasing, backlight and damage behavior require GPU review
color is artistic interpretation rather than historical documentation
